problems.title: Batch-1 decode
problems.statement: 7B in BF16 on an H100 (3.35 TB/s).
problems.solution: About 4.2 ms and 240 tokens/s, an upper bound that ignores the KV and overheads.

problems.title: KV cache

parts.prompt: KB per token with 32 KV heads (MHA)?
KB per token with 8 KV heads (GQA)?

problems.solution: 512 KB vs 128 KB per token; 2 GiB per 4k-token sequence with MHA.

problems.title: Max batch
problems.statement: 80 GB H100, 14 GB weights, 6 GB overhead, MHA KV at 0.5 MB/token, 4,096-token contexts.
problems.solution: About 27–30 vs about 110. GQA's whole point is serving batch size.

problems.title: Prefill
problems.statement: A 2,000-token prompt into a 7B model; achieved 400 TFLOP/s.

problems.title: Crossover
problems.statement: H100: 989 TFLOP/s, 3.35 TB/s, BF16 weights (2 bytes/param, 2 FLOPs/param/token).

parts.prompt: Decode batch where weight-bound compute ≈ memory time (balance × 2 bytes / 2 FLOPs)?

hints: Per decode step, each 2-byte weight is read once and used for B multiply-adds (2B FLOPs): intensity ≈ B FLOPs/byte.
problems.solution: About 295: below that batch, BF16 decode is memory-bound (ignoring the KV reads, which push it further).

problems.title: Quantisation
problems.statement: Switching weights from BF16 to INT4 for batch-1 decode.

options: dequantisation overhead, KV reads not shrunk, kernel efficiency

problems.solution: Up to 4× fewer weight bytes; real gains are often 2–3×.

problems.title: Speculative decoding
problems.statement: A draft proposes k = 4 tokens; on average 3 are accepted. The big model's verification pass costs about one decode step; the draft costs 10% of a step per token.
